summary.text: 体 is the simplified Chinese form used for 體, “body.” The shape 体 also has a separately recorded reading bèn, “coarse; inferior,” but the evidence does not establish that this use developed into the body-character spelling.

formation.text: For the body word, 体 functions as a simplified counterpart and historical variant of 體; its visible parts 亻 and 本 do not by themselves establish how the body character was formed. A separate bèn entry is analyzed as 人 plus 本, with 本 phonetic, but this is an editorial analysis, not verified by early graphic evidence. The traditional 體 is analyzed in the received Shuowen account as 骨 plus 豊, with 豊 phonetic; that account is historical testimony rather than independent proof of origin.

history.text: The evidence reports 體 in a late Warring States bronze example and in later script forms, but does not establish its earliest attestation. A seal-script-style image in the dossier is a modern redraw of a received Shuowen-style form, not an excavated artifact.

Dictionaries record 体 as a vulgar variant of 體, including examples from Song–Yuan onward, and identify it as the standardized simplified counterpart. They do not establish the exact route from the older variant to standardization. Longkan Shoujian is reported to write it as ⿰亻夲, but this does not prove that 本 was a historical sound component.

uncertainties.text: The evidence distinguishes 体 bèn, “coarse; inferior,” from 体 tǐ as a variant spelling of 體. It does not establish whether the two uses are historically connected, or verify the bèn analysis through early paleographic evidence.

No exact earliest dated use of 體 or 体 is established here. The evidence also does not verify a same-system historical sound comparison for 豊 and 體, or the precise standardization path of simplified 体.

senses.text: 体 is recorded as a variant spelling of 體, whose documented senses include the whole human or animal body and limbs. The consulted evidence does not date the earliest use of this sense.
A separate bèn reading of 体 is recorded with the sense “coarse; inferior,” equated with 笨. Its relation, if any, to the tǐ spelling of 體 is not established.

limitations.text: The recorded body, substance, essential form, and writing-style senses belong to 體 in the supplied evidence; no dated sequence or semantic path among them is established here. Compound glosses and dictionary lists alone do not establish additional single-character senses of 体.
The evidence does not identify an earliest attested use for either sense listed here, and does not show that the bèn and tǐ uses share a history.

overview.text: 体 is the simplified form used for 體, “body.” The same shape is also recorded separately as bèn, “coarse; inferior”; its connection to the body spelling is unproven.

relationships.text: 体 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 體 and was also recorded as a traditional vulgar variant; the precise route to standardization is not documented in the evidence.
